clinicalNotes.title: Orthopedic Trauma H&P: Right Femoral Neck Fracture
clinicalNotes.text:
80-year-old female tripped over a rug sustaining right hip pain and inability to bear weight.
Radiographs show subcapital displaced right femoral neck fracture.
Scheduled for urgent right cemented hemiarthroplasty. Scheduled Acetaminophen 650 mg q6h. Oxycodone 5-10 mg q4h PRN prescribed for post-op severe breakthrough pain.

clinicalNotes.title: Operative & Post-Op Day 1 Note
clinicalNotes.text: Right hemiarthroplasty completed without surgical complications. Hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL. Pain controlled with Oxycodone 10 mg every 4 hours.

clinicalNotes.title: Nursing Shift Note: Acute Delirium & Agitation
clinicalNotes.text:
CONTRADICTORY RECORD:
Nurse reports: "Patient acutely confused, thrashing in bed, attempting to climb out of bed, pulling at Foley catheter and IV line. Screaming that spiders and insects are crawling across the ceiling. Visual hallucinations present. CAM-ICU positive for delirium."
clinicalNotes.metaAnnotation: Contradiction: Nursing documents acute hallucinations and severe delirium.

clinicalNotes.title: Surgical Resident / Physician Cross-Cover Note
clinicalNotes.text:
CONTRADICTORY RECORD:
Physician writes 45 minutes later: "Patient is resting quietly in bed, alert and oriented x 3, pleasant and cooperative, answering all questions appropriately with zero evidence of agitation or confusion."
(NOTE: Striking clinical discrepancy with nursing report NOTE-503).
clinicalNotes.metaAnnotation: Severe contradiction: Physician claims patient is alert x3 with zero confusion 45m after nursing reports hallucinations.

clinicalNotes.title: Geriatric Medicine Consultation: Delirium & Analgesic Adjustment
clinicalNotes.text:
Geriatrics consulted for post-operative delirium.
Assessment: Opioid-induced delirium / hallucinations likely exacerbated by full mu-opioid agonist Oxycodone in an elderly patient with borderline cognitive reserve.
MEDICATION CHANGE:
1. Oxycodone is completely DISCONTINUED.
2. Switched to low-dose Tramadol 25 mg q6h PRN only for severe breakthrough pain.
3. Maximize scheduled Acetaminophen 650 mg q6h. Implement delirium precautions, daytime sunlight exposure, family presence.
clinicalNotes.metaAnnotation: Explains discontinuation of Oxycodone and switch to low-dose Tramadol.

clinicalNotes.title: Discharge Summary - ADM-501 Hip Repair & Rehab Transfer
clinicalNotes.text:
Delirium cleared completely following Oxycodone discontinuation. Mentation at baseline.
Transferred to Subacute Rehabilitation facility for physical therapy.

clinicalNotes.title: H&P: Acute Anticholinergic Toxicity & Urinary Retention
clinicalNotes.text:
Patient brought to emergency department by daughter for acute confusion, speech stumbling, dilated pupils, dry flushed skin, and lower abdominal distension.
Bladder scan reveals 850 mL acute urinary retention. Foley catheter placed with immediate relief.
Medication reconciliation reveals patient was self-administering over-the-counter Diphenhydramine (Benadryl) 50 mg every night for severe insomnia over the past 2 weeks.
Diagnosis: Anticholinergic toxidrome and urinary retention secondary to Diphenhydramine in high-risk elderly patient.

clinicalNotes.title: Medicine Progress Note: Anticholinergic Washout
clinicalNotes.text: Benadryl discontinued immediately. Cognitive symptoms and confusion resolving rapidly as anticholinergic clears. Foley removed, voiding spontaneously. Initiated Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime for non-anticholinergic insomnia management.

clinicalNotes.title: Discharge Summary - ADM-502 Benadryl Discontinuation
clinicalNotes.text: Patient discharged home in stable condition. Daughter educated on Beers Criteria medications and dangerous anticholinergics (Benadryl, dimenhydrinate) to strictly avoid in elderly patients.
